newsitem.title: UK: Sick workers cost British business 12 bln stg -CBI.
newsitem.headline: Sick workers cost British business 12 bln stg -CBI.

text.p: Employees on sick leave cost British business some 12 billion pounds last year, top employers group the Confederation of British Industry said on Tuesday.
A survey by the CBI estimated 187 million working days were lost due to sickness absence -- an average of 8.4 working days for every employee, or 3.7 percent of the total working hours over the year.
John Cridland, the CBI's director of human resources, said sick leave was costing more than it did in 1994. Then absences averaged 7.8 days per employee.
"To cut these costs firms need to encourage their management to take a more active role in managing workplace attendance."
He said first line managers must monitor absenteeism and advised the introduction of "family-friendly" policies such as flexible leave and childcare support could help cut the number of days lost.
